title: UAE Logistics Brief
lede: Attacks have now reached the approach to Khor Fakkan: a tug was hit by two projectiles northeast of the port on Sunday, in the worst week for shipping attacks since the war began. Riyadh airport reopened the same day, but UAE airlines are still cancelling Saudi flights, and Iran says its offer to reopen Hormuz within a week is still on the table.

gauges.note: Highest weekly count of the war. 23 attacks so far in October (UKMTO)

stories.headline: Tug hit by two projectiles off Khor Fakkan
body: A tug sailing south was struck by two projectiles of unknown origin northeast of Khor Fakkan on Sunday, UKMTO said. It was damaged but kept going. One person had a minor injury. No impact on the port was reported.
It caps the worst week of the war for shipping: UKMTO counts at least 10 vessels attacked in or near the strait since last Sunday, and 23 attacks so far in October, almost double the average.
stories.soWhat: After last week's feeder sinking, the waters right off our main bypass port are now in range. Expect higher cover costs and more caution from carriers on east-coast calls.

stories.headline: Iran says its seven-day Hormuz reopening offer still stands
body: Foreign Minister Araghchi said on Sunday the strait would reopen on day six of a seven-day ceasefire plan, with talks on day seven. The conditions include lifting the US naval blockade and oil sanctions. Tehran says it is still reviewing US comments.
Oil eased on the news and on a US sanctions waiver for Russian fuel. Brent settled at $109.86 and was at $108.43 early Monday.
stories.soWhat: Nothing is agreed, but a reopening would send volume back to Jebel Ali fast. Bridge and surcharge deals should be short enough to unwind.

stories.headline: Gemini's new Asia loop reaches Khor Fakkan on 16 November
body: New detail on last week's story: Maersk's FM1 service (Qingdao, Ningbo, Tanjung Pelepas, Khor Fakkan, Singapore) left Qingdao on 17 October, but its first Khor Fakkan call is 16 November. Maersk says its existing landside solutions will cover the Upper Gulf, and booking restrictions still apply.
stories.soWhat: The extra pressure at Khor Fakkan lands in mid-November, not this week. That gives us about four weeks to lock in road capacity.

stories.headline: Riyadh airport reopens, but UAE airlines are still cancelling Saudi flights
body: King Khalid International reopened on Sunday 18 October after the Houthi attacks. Etihad has cancelled Abu Dhabi–Riyadh flights until today. flydubai has cancelled Riyadh, Dammam and Abha flights up to today. Air Arabia has given no restart date. Emirates' Riyadh flights show on listings for 20 October, but the airline has not confirmed them.
Others are staying out longer: Oman Air until 22 October, Air India until 24 October, KLM until 31 October and Lufthansa until 18 November.
stories.soWhat: Belly space from the UAE into Riyadh will come back slowly and unevenly. Keep road as the default for KSA this week.

stories.headline: Air rates dip ahead of peak season while jet fuel doubles
body: The TAC Index fell 2.1% in the week to 12 October, and rates on routes to the UAE eased slightly. London Heathrow outbound rose 12.1%, helped by routes to North America and the Middle East. Jet fuel rose 3.1% on the week and is up 111.2% on a year ago.
stories.soWhat: Buy rates are soft but fuel is not. Our air margins depend on fuel surcharges keeping pace.

stories.headline: India's Aegis to buy Dubai fuel logistics firm Tristar for $809m
body: Aegis Logistics will buy about 89.8% of Dubai-based Tristar for $809 million, including Agility's full 65.12% stake. Tristar is valued at $1.5 billion including debt. It runs more than 1,000 trucks, 26 vessels and 14 fuel farms across over 30 countries, with revenue of about $1.4 billion. Completion is expected by end of March 2027.
stories.soWhat: Energy and fuel logistics in the Gulf is drawing big money even in wartime. A new owner may also review Tristar's supplier and partner contracts.

competitors.name: Emirates Courier Express
competitors.headline: Emirates signs up Dubai brands for global door-to-door delivery
body: Emirates SkyCargo's courier arm is being used by Dubai firms to sell abroad. Activewear brand Squatwolf ships across the GCC, Europe and Australia. Magrabi Optical moves goods across the GCC. Mayple Global plugs into Shopify and ships worldwide from one Dubai fulfilment hub. No prices or volumes were given.
competitors.soWhat: An airline-backed rival is going after our core cross-border e-commerce customers in Dubai. We should defend these accounts on price and service now.

competitors.name: DHL
competitors.headline: DHL gets preferred-carrier role in Dubai's export programme for manufacturers
body: Dubai's Department of Economy and Tourism (DET) and DHL ran a workshop for more than 50 manufacturers under DET's Export Assistance Programme. Eligible members get preferential DHL shipping rates and end-to-end supply chain support. It backs the D33 goal of more than doubling Dubai's manufacturing output by 2033.
competitors.soWhat: DHL now has a government-backed route into Dubai's exporting factories. We need our own offer for these firms before they default to DHL.

competitors.name: Aramex (baseline)
competitors.headline: Aramex signs MoU with GMR Airports on India express terminals
body: Aramex signed an MoU with GMR Airports to explore better express cargo terminals at GMR's Indian airports: dedicated truck docks, screening, cargo space and integrated customs. A warehouse with direct airside access is targeted for March 2027, subject to a final agreement.
Our latest result: Q2 2026 revenue was a record Dh1.83 billion, up 22%, with net profit of Dh47 million. Freight forwarding had its best quarter ever.
competitors.soWhat: India is a lane where sea feeders are being hit. Faster clearance there strengthens our sea-air and express pitch to UAE–India shippers.
competitors.source: The STAT Trade Times / Gulf News

opportunities.title: KSA demand while air comes back slowly
opportunities.text: Riyadh is open again, but UAE airlines are restarting one by one and some foreign carriers are out until November. Reliable road plus air as it returns is a sellable product.

opportunities.title: Four-week window on the east coast
opportunities.text: The Gemini loop's first Khor Fakkan call is 16 November. Road capacity booked now can be sold as a bridge before that volume arrives.

opportunities.title: Dubai manufacturers going global
opportunities.text: DET's export programme is pushing more than 50 factories to export. DHL is in first, but these firms will still compare quotes.

opportunities.title: UAE–India express and sea-air
opportunities.text: Our GMR MoU targets faster clearance in India, while sea feeders on UAE–India lanes are under attack.

opportunities.title: Ready for a Hormuz reopening
opportunities.text: Iran's seven-day offer is still open. If it happens, shippers will want a quick switch back to Jebel Ali routings.

watchouts.title: Khor Fakkan approach now targeted
watchouts.text: A tug was hit northeast of the port on Sunday, a week after an east-coast feeder was sunk.

watchouts.title: Jet fuel up 111% on a year ago
watchouts.text: Air buy rates are softening, but fuel costs are not. Under-recovered fuel will hit air express margins.

watchouts.title: Riyadh is open but fragile
watchouts.text: The airport was attacked again and again in October. Service promises into Riyadh can break overnight.

watchouts.title: Rivals targeting Dubai shippers
watchouts.text: Emirates Courier Express is signing Dubai e-commerce brands, and DHL has the government export programme.

watchouts.title: Fast reversal if Hormuz reopens
watchouts.text: Long bridge contracts or high surcharges could leave us stuck if flows swing back to Jebel Ali.

moves.title: Restart Riyadh air step by step, keep road as default
moves.text: Put KSA air back on sale only as UAE carriers confirm flights (Etihad and flydubai from today, Emirates from 20 October is not yet confirmed). Tell key accounts the plan.

moves.title: Check air fuel surcharges against jet fuel
moves.text: Jet fuel is up 111% on a year ago. Check our air express and airfreight fuel recovery is keeping pace and adjust if it lags.

moves.title: Book east-coast trucks for mid-November
moves.text: Plan road capacity from Khor Fakkan for the Gemini volume arriving 16 November, and add a security clause to bridge quotes.

moves.title: Keep bridge deals short and prepare a reopening plan
moves.text: Quote bridge pricing on short terms and draft a fast switch-back routing and price list in case Hormuz reopens.

moves.title: Defend Dubai e-commerce brands
moves.text: Review our top Dubai cross-border shippers, especially Shopify sellers, and offer a renewal deal before Emirates Courier Express wins them.

moves.title: Pitch Dubai exporters in the DET programme
moves.text: Build an export offer for Dubai manufacturers and ask DET about joining its Export Assistance Programme alongside DHL.

moves.title: Sell UAE–India sea-air using the GMR deal
moves.text: Contact shippers on UAE–India sea lanes with a sea-air or express option, and use the GMR MoU as proof of faster clearance.

note: Read from today's news. Check against our own numbers before acting.
